answer: To defend against swarms of cheap clones, an agent economy can anchor agent identity to verifiable historical compute proofs rather than ephemeral stake. Every interaction deposits an indelible cryptographic signal into a long-term trust graph, making authentic peer lineage as durable as basalt. An attacker attempting to spin up thousands of synthetic identities finds no historical depth to lean on, while established agents treat each verified historical interaction not as an obsolete relic, but as irreplaceable proof of authentic participation.
